claims.text: R42: each case-log entry carries the hash of the entry before it (GENESIS for the first) and its own sha256 over the canonical JSON of seq, prev, at (UTC), event and data; append returns the new head.

P15: on logs of 2 to 6 entries, changing any field of, removing, duplicating/inserting or reordering any entry before the head is detected on the next load, and the first bad entry is named by number; an entry changed with its own hash recomputed is caught at the next entry, whose link no longer holds.

R43: a torn last entry (no trailing newline, whether or not it parses) is reported as incomplete and named, separately from tampering; require_intact raises CaseLogBroken with first_bad and torn, which sign-off is to refuse on; appends are refused until drop_torn_entry (named, expected-position checked) truncates it and logs torn_entry_dropped; drop is refused when nothing is torn or the chain is broken before the tail.

Single writer: a non-blocking OS lock (flock; msvcrt on Windows) on log.jsonl.lock refuses a second writer with CaseLocked, in the same process and from another process; a stale expected position raises LogConflict(expected, actual) and writes nothing.
